s1.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous mass in the lower abdominal region with cyclical pain
salient_findings: Subcutaneous nodule approximately 1 cm in diameter
key_facts: 39-year-old female patient
Subcutaneous mass in the lower-left abdominal region
History of chronic urticaria
History of cesarean section eight years ago
History of myomectomy six months ago
No history of dysmenorrhea or abortion
Slight pain accompanying the mass
Pain worsens around menstruation
Linear scar in the lower-left abdominal region
Ultrasonography showed a hybrid echo-mass
Histopathology revealed endometrial glands and stroma

raw.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous mass in the lower abdominal region with cyclical pain

shortlist.label: Endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology revealed endometrial glands and stroma, and pain worsens around menstruation

shortlist.label: Subcutaneous myoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of myomectomy and presence of a subcutaneous mass

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasonography showed a hybrid echo-mass, which could be consistent with a vascularized lipoma

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous mass with slight pain, and histopathology could be consistent with a benign proliferative process

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: History of previous surgeries and presence of a subcutaneous mass, which could be consistent with a desmoid tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of endometrial glands and stroma in the histopathology, along with the worsening of pain around menstruation, strongly supports the diagnosis of endometriosis, which is a condition where endometrial tissue grows outside the uterus.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous myoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of myomectomy, the histopathology does not show characteristics of a myoma, but rather endometrial glands and stroma.

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: The ultrasonography and histopathology do not indicate a lipoma or a vascular tumor, which are characteristic of angiolipoma.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis
rejected.why: The histopathology does not show the typical features of nodular fasciitis, such as a benign proliferation of fibroblasts and inflammatory cells.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: The histopathology does not indicate a desmoid tumor, which typically shows a proliferation of well-differentiated fibroblasts without the presence of endometrial glands and stroma.
